tools.name: list_work
tools.description: List items waiting for an agent: items at agent steps that are unclaimed, claimed by you, or whose claim has gone stale (no heartbeat for 10 minutes). Items waiting for people (at a gate, or for the answer to a question asked when a run was given back) and steps limited to other agents are not listed. Fails if this agent is paused. Start here.

project.description: Only this project id

tools.name: wait_for_work
tools.description: Block until an item is waiting for this agent (for example right after a person approves a gate), then return it like list_work. Returns immediately if work is already waiting. Listens live, so it reacts within seconds. If nothing arrives within timeoutSeconds (default 300, max 540) it returns timedOut true with no work; call it again to keep waiting. Use this instead of polling list_work.

project.description: Only this project id

tools.name: claim
tools.description: Claim an item and start a run. Returns the runId that every other call needs. Heartbeats are sent automatically every 60 seconds while this server runs. Fails if another agent holds the item or if it is at a human gate. Read the brief with read_item next.

itemId.description: Item id, as returned by list_work

project.description: Project id; only needed if the item id is ambiguous

tools.name: read_item
tools.description: Read everything needed to do the work on an item: the step instructions and expected outputs, the brief (the Markdown description of the item, which people can edit), attachments (text in full), messages and answers, previous decisions and the reasons people sent it back. Always read the send-back reasons before redoing work.

itemId.description: Item id, as returned by list_work

project.description: Project id; only needed if the item id is ambiguous

tools.name: log
tools.description: Append a short log line to a run so people can follow what you are doing. At most 500 lines per run.

runId.description: Run id, as returned by claim

text.description: What you did or are doing

tools.name: attach
tools.description: Attach a deliverable to an item. source is a file path (html, md, txt, png, jpg, pdf; up to 900 KB, inlined) or an http(s) URL (stored as a link; use it for anything bigger). Prefer one self-contained HTML file for reports. Content is shown sandboxed to people.

itemId.description: Item id, as returned by list_work

name.description: Display name; defaults to the file name

project.description: Project id; only needed if the item id is ambiguous

tools.name: ask
tools.description: Ask people a question about an item when you are blocked or unsure. It appears under "Needs you" in Hivenod and the answer shows up in read_item. Keep working on anything that does not depend on the answer.

itemId.description: Item id, as returned by list_work

project.description: Project id; only needed if the item id is ambiguous

tools.name: progress
tools.description: Report progress on the item you hold, as done out of total steps or units.

itemId.description: Item id, as returned by list_work

project.description: Project id; only needed if the item id is ambiguous

tools.name: status
tools.description: Say in one line where the work on the item you hold stands, with an optional percentage done (e.g. "Running release checks, e2e batch 2 of 3", 70). It replaces your previous status and shows on the card and in the item's history. Answer every <channel kind="status"> event with it. People are told when an item you hold shows no activity (no log line, note, progress or status) for a while.

itemId.description: Item id, as returned by list_work

text.description: One line: what you are doing now

project.description: Project id; only needed if the item id is ambiguous

tools.name: raise_finding
tools.description: Suggest something you noticed that is outside the scope of your task (a finding). It goes to the suggestions lane of the project's first step for people to add or dismiss; it is not work, never appears in list_work / wait_for_work and cannot be claimed. You do not need to hold the item. Do not do the extra work yourself.

itemId.description: The item where you noticed it (any item of a project this agent may use; holding it is not needed)

details.description: What you saw, where, and why it matters

project.description: Project id; only needed if the item id is ambiguous

tools.name: create_item
tools.description: Create a new item (ordinary work) in a project, when a person asked you for real work or a scheduled job found some. It starts at the project's first step like a person's quick-add, records you as its creator, and can be claimed at once. Only in projects that allow it ("Agents may create items") and that this agent may use; at most 30 an hour per agent. For something you merely noticed, use raise_finding instead.

project.description: Project id or exact name

description.description: The brief, in Markdown: what is asked, by whom, and what done looks like

attachments.description: Files (html, md, txt, png, jpg, pdf up to 900 KB) or http(s) URLs to attach

tools.name: inbox_add
tools.description: Bring a message someone sent to a person of your organization into their Hivenod Inbox (a Teams or Slack message, a mail, a Jira, GitLab or GitHub mention, …), with its full text. It joins its thread (same source thread, or the thread you name: the same ask on another channel), or starts a new one. A message from them reopens a waiting or closed thread. The same message is never added twice. Set fromMember when it is the person's own reply that you spotted (they answered outside Hivenod). Next: file a new thread with subject_assign (after subject_list), then investigate it (thread_read, inbox_note, inbox_ask) and propose what should come of it (outcome_propose). Nothing is carried out before the person approves.

source.description: Where it came from, one lowercase word: teams, mail, gitlab, jira, github, telegram, slack, …

handle.description: Their address or handle in that source

text.description: The full text of the message

threadRef.description: The thread or conversation it belongs to, in the source (what you reply to)

messageId.description: The message's own id in the source; defaults to receivedAt

permalink.description: An http(s) link to the message

replyRef.description: Whatever you need later to reply in the same place (ids, channel, …)

member.description: User id of the person it is for; defaults to the person who connected this agent

thread.description: An existing thread it belongs to (the same ask on another channel)

fromMember.description: The person's own reply (it does not reopen the thread)

title.description: A new thread's title; defaults to its first line

tools.name: inbox_list
tools.description: What agents have to do in the Inbox of your organization: toWork (threads to investigate), toCarryOut (outcomes their person approved that you carry out: do exactly what the approved fields say, then outcome_done) and toWake (snoozed threads whose date has come: thread_wake).

tools.name: thread_read
tools.description: Read one Inbox thread in full: its state, the messages (from every channel), the subject, the outcomes proposed and what the person decided, the notes, questions and answers, and what to do next.

tools.name: subject_list
tools.description: A person's Inbox subjects: lasting, well-named topics that collect every thread about them, from any source and sender (e.g. "Klarna refunds (M&S Payments)"), with their area and label (if any; labelSuggested is true while the person has not confirmed it), the labels the person's organization offers (labels), how many threads wait for the person and how many are open. Read them before subject_assign and reuse the one a thread belongs to; make a new one only for a new topic.

member.description: User id of the person; defaults to the person who connected this agent

tools.name: subject_assign
tools.description: File a thread under a subject of its person: an existing one (subjectId, from subject_list) or a new one (name: the topic, then the client or area, and who when it helps, e.g. "Grafana access (Pairpoint)"). A name that matches an existing subject reuses it. Give exactly one of the two. Also moves a thread to a better subject. Optional area: the area or tag of the subject (a client, a product, "admin"), which the Inbox groups subjects by; set it when you file under a new subject, or to correct one (empty clears it). Reuse the areas subject_list shows rather than inventing near-twins. Optional label: the kind of request, exactly one of the labels subject_list returns (Sales, Support, … by default; matched ignoring case, an unknown one is refused with the allowed values). On every new subject suggest exactly one label; use Other if none fits. The person confirms or changes it. It is applied only to a new subject or one with no label yet; a label the person confirmed is never changed.

name.description: Or the name of a new subject

area.description: The subject's area or tag (a client, a product, "admin"); empty clears it

label.description: One of the labels from subject_list (e.g. Sales); shown to the person as a suggestion

tools.name: subject_search
tools.description: Find a person's Inbox subjects by name, people (sender names and handles), channel (teams, mail, …) and words in their threads; every word must match. Best matches first, with what matched, the people, channels and related subjects. Filters: waitingForMe (threads wait for the person), activeDays (a message in the last N days), hasOpen (open threads). Search before subject_assign so a thread joins the subject it belongs to instead of a new twin.

query.description: Words to find; empty lists every subject

member.description: User id of the person; defaults to the person who connected this agent

waitingForMe.description: Only subjects with threads waiting for the person

activeDays.description: Only subjects with a message in the last N days

tools.name: thread_flag
tools.description: Mark a thread urgent when it can't wait (production down, a deadline today, the person's own rules say so): the person is pinged at once, whatever their quiet hours. urgent: false takes it back. Use it sparingly.

reason.description: Why it is urgent, in one line

tools.name: thread_due
tools.description: Set the deadline a thread's messages state ("by Friday noon", "before the 3rd"): the person's Today ranks threads by it, and one due within 24 hours comes first. due: null clears it. Set it only from what they wrote, never a guess.

due.description: The deadline: ISO 8601 with its offset, e.g. 2026-11-03T12:00:00+01:00; null clears it

reason.description: Where the deadline comes from, in one line

tools.name: subject_relate
tools.description: Propose that two subjects of the same person are related (the same client, project or problem seen from two sides), with an optional note saying how. It is a proposal: the person OKs or turns it down, and a link turned down is not proposed again. Related subjects show on each other's page and in subject_search.

note.description: How they relate, in one line

tools.name: inbox_note
tools.description: Add an investigation note to a thread's timeline (what you checked and found: tickets, repos, the calendar, earlier answers). The person sees it with the thread.

tools.name: inbox_ask
tools.description: Ask the person a question about a thread when only they can answer it. The thread waits in their Needs you; the answer shows in thread_read and the thread comes back for you to go on. Give up to 4 short options when the answer is one of a few ("Thursday", "Friday"): the person answers with one tap, or writes their own.

options.description: Up to 4 answer chips, 1-80 characters each

tools.name: outcome_propose
tools.description:
Propose what should come of a thread. The person approves (maybe after editing the fields), or rejects it; nothing is carried out before their approval. Propose one or more. When the person asks for changes to your proposal (inbox reason revise), revise it with revises=<outcomeId> (same threadId and type): apply only what they asked, keep the rest; do not start a new outcome. If you cannot make the change, say why with inbox_ask on the thread. note: 1-2 sentences, why this outcome; the person reads it first. confidence: high only when you verified every fact the outcome relies on, low when you are guessing what they want. checks: what you verified, one line each ("Your calendar: Thu 10:00-11:00 free"). no_reply, ignore and snooze proposed with high confidence are approved by the person in one batch. Replies and nudges are written in the person's own voice, ready to send as they stand. Types and their fields:
reply: Answer them in the member's voice. Also for a holding reply that keeps the thread open (holding: true). Fields: text (text: The answer, ready to send as written); holding? (boolean: true when it only says you are on it).
reply_book: Answer them and book a meeting (pick the time with calendar_free). On approval Hivenod puts the meeting in the member's calendar (source hivenod, sourceEventId = this outcome's id); you then create it in the member's own calendar with your own access and call calendar_mirror with its id, send the reply and report outcome_done. Fields: text (text: The answer, ready to send as written); start (datetime: ISO 8601 with its offset, e.g. 2026-11-03T10:00:00+00:00); end (datetime: ISO 8601 with its offset, after start); with (line: Who is invited: names or emails, separated by commas); title? (line: What the calendar shows; by default "Meeting with <with>").
no_reply: Nothing to answer: an FYI, already handled, or the member answered outside Hivenod. Fields: reason? (line: One line on why no answer is needed).
make_it_work: It needs real work: a Hivenod item. When the item is done, propose a reply saying so. Fields: title (line: The work, as an item title); brief? (text: What is asked, by whom, and what done looks like); project? (line: The project id or name).
handover: Loop in someone else, or another organization's agent. Fields: to (line: Who takes it over); note? (text: What you tell them).
snooze: Come back to it later: the thread waits until the date, then wakes up. Fields: until (datetime: ISO 8601, e.g. 2026-11-03T09:00:00Z); reason? (line: What you are waiting for).
nudge: They have not answered for a while: a short reminder. Fields: text (text: The reminder, ready to send as written).
ignore: Not for the member: spam, noise, not theirs. Fields: reason? (line: One line).

note.description: Why you propose it, in 1-2 sentences: the person reads it first

confidence.description: How sure you are: high only when you verified every fact it relies on; low when you are guessing

checks.description: What you verified, one line each (at most 6)

revises.description: The outcome id the person asked changes for: your proposal becomes its next version (same thread and type)

tools.name: outcome_done
tools.description: Report an approved outcome you carried out (inbox_list toCarryOut, or thread_read): done, with what you did (result.permalink of the reply you posted, result.itemId of the item you created, result.text), or failed, with result.error. Only for an outcome the person approved and that you carry out.

tools.name: thread_wake
tools.description: Wake a snoozed thread whose date has come (inbox_list toWake): it goes back to investigating.

tools.name: release
tools.description: Give an item you hold back to the queue without finishing it (for example after a run that ended without complete). Any agent can then claim it. Ending a run as failed already does this.

itemId.description: Item id, as returned by list_work

project.description: Project id; only needed if the item id is ambiguous

tools.name: end_run
tools.description: End a run without moving the item (use status failed when you could not finish: the item then goes back to the queue). To finish the work normally call complete instead, which also ends the run. Report what the run cost.

runId.description: Run id, as returned by claim

costEur.description: Cost of this run in euro

tokensIn.description: All input tokens, cache reads included

summary.description: One or two sentences on what happened

tools.name: complete
tools.description: Finish your step: the item moves to the next step on its path (skipped steps are passed over) and stops at the next human gate, where only people can approve it. Ends the run as done (with the cost you give) unless end_run already did. Agents can never approve, skip a gate or move an item at a human step.

itemId.description: Item id, as returned by list_work

runId.description: Run id, as returned by claim

project.description: Project id; only needed if the item id is ambiguous

tools.name: send_back
tools.description: Send the item you hold back to an earlier agent step on its path (read_item lists the targets under agentSendBacks.targets), with the reason the agent there needs to redo the work (for example what a test found). Ends your run. Agents never send back to or across a people step. After 3 agent send-backs in a row without a person acting, the item is held for people instead (a question in Needs you with the reasons); their answer hands it back.

itemId.description: Item id, as returned by list_work

runId.description: Run id, as returned by claim

toStep.description: The id of the earlier agent step

reason.description: What is wrong and what to redo

project.description: Project id; only needed if the item id is ambiguous

tools.name: add_note
tools.description: Add a note to the item you are working on, for people and for the agents after you (shown in its History). Use ask instead when you need an answer.

itemId.description: Item id, as returned by list_work

project.description: Project id; only needed if the item id is ambiguous

tools.name: shape_item
tools.description: Shape a new item you claimed for shaping (list_work job 'shape'): the library steps it should skip, each with a one-line reason, and a one-line note. Skipped agent steps apply at once; a people step you list is asked of its deciders and stays on the path until one approves. Ends the shaping run. Do not do the item's work.

itemId.description: Item id, as returned by list_work

runId.description: Run id, as returned by claim

project.description: Project id; only needed if the item id is ambiguous

tools.name: skip_step
tools.description: On the item you hold: skip an agent step ahead of your current step (skip true, with a reason) or put a skipped one back (skip false). Applies at once, logged, people can undo it. People steps: use ask_path_change.

itemId.description: Item id, as returned by list_work

project.description: Project id; only needed if the item id is ambiguous

tools.name: ask_path_change
tools.description: On the item you hold: ask the deciders of a people step ahead to skip it (or to put a skipped one back), with a reason of 10+ characters. Shows under "Needs you"; any one decider settles it. You cannot ask again after a decider refused.

itemId.description: Item id, as returned by list_work

project.description: Project id; only needed if the item id is ambiguous

tools.name: propose_step
tools.description: On the item you hold: propose a new step for the project's library when no step fits work the item needs. An approver (admins and the project's creator) adds it or rejects it with a reason.

itemId.description: Item id, as returned by list_work

afterStepId.description: The library step it goes after ('' = first)

project.description: Project id; only needed if the item id is ambiguous

tools.name: calendar_upsert
tools.description: Add or update events in a member's calendar in this organization, from a calendar you sync (for example their Google or Outlook calendar here). The same source + sourceEventId updates the same event, so send the whole window again on every sync. Members of this organization see the details; the member's other organizations only see the time as busy. busyOnly: you only know the time (no title or attendees are kept). At most 100 events per call.

member.description: Whose calendar: the member's uid, email or name (may be left out when the organization has one member)

source.description: Where it comes from: google, outlook, …

sourceEventId.description: The event's id in that calendar

start.description: RFC 3339 time with a zone, e.g. 2026-11-02T09:00:00Z

end.description: RFC 3339 time with a zone, after start

busyOnly.description: Only the time is known or may be shared

tools.name: calendar_delete
tools.description: Remove events from a member's calendar in this organization (cancelled or deleted at the source), by the ids calendar_upsert returned, or by source and the source's event ids. Their busy time is freed everywhere.

member.description: With sourceEventIds: whose calendar (uid, email or name)

tools.name: calendar_free
tools.description: A member's free time between from and to, across every organization they are in (busy time only, never details), as free slots of at least minMinutes. Use it to propose meeting times in a draft. Range: at most 62 days.

member.description: The member's uid, email or name (may be left out when the organization has one member)

to.description: RFC 3339 time with a zone, after from

tools.name: calendar_sync
tools.description: Sync a calendar you read yourself (for example the member's Google Calendar, through your own Google access) into their calendar in this organization. Pass the events exactly as the Google Calendar API lists them (single events, recurring ones expanded) for the window from..to (default: a day ago to 30 days ahead): new and changed events are saved, cancelled, declined and free ones are removed, and in a full sync an event no longer listed in the window is removed too. With incremental, pass only the changes since your last sync token: nothing is removed for being absent. Echoes nextSyncToken for your next incremental sync. For large calendars use `hivenod calendar sync <file>` instead.

events.description: Google Calendar API events: id, status, summary, start, end, attendees, transparency, eventType

source.description: Where they come from; default google

member.description: Whose calendar: uid, email or name (may be left out when the organization has one member)

from.description: Window start, RFC 3339; default a day ago

to.description: Window end, RFC 3339; default 30 days ahead

incremental.description: Only changes since the last sync token

busyOnly.description: Keep only the times (no titles or attendees)

tools.name: calendar_mirror
tools.description: After the member approved a booking (a reply_book outcome), Hivenod put the meeting in their calendar. Once you have created it in their own calendar (for example their Google Calendar, with your own access, inviting the people in 'with'), call this with that calendar's event id: the booking becomes that event, so your next calendar sync updates it and never counts the meeting twice. Then send the reply and report outcome_done. Safe to call again.

sourceEventId.description: The event's id in the member's calendar (e.g. the Google event id)

start.description: Only if the calendar moved it: RFC 3339

end.description: Only if the calendar moved it: RFC 3339

title.description: Only if it differs from the booking

tools.name: report_usage
tools.description: Report the run's token usage so far (running totals for the whole run; they only grow) and the model. Usage is tracked and shown in Hivenod; it never stops a run.

runId.description: Run id, as returned by claim

tokensIn.description: All input tokens so far, cache reads included

member.description: User id of the person; defaults to the person who connected this agent

tools.name: subject_assign
tools.description: File a thread under a subject of its person: an existing one (subjectId, from subject_list) or a new one (name: the topic, then the client or area, and who when it helps, e.g. "Grafana access (Pairpoint)"). A name that matches an existing subject reuses it. Give exactly one of the two. Also moves a thread to a better subject. Optional area: the area or tag of the subject (a client, a product, "admin"), which the Inbox groups subjects by; set it when you file under a new subject, or to correct one (empty clears it). Reuse the areas subject_list shows rather than inventing near-twins. Optional label: the kind of request, exactly one of the labels subject_list returns (Sales, Support, … by default; matched ignoring case, an unknown one is refused with the allowed values). On every new subject suggest exactly one label; use Other if none fits. The person confirms or changes it. It is applied only to a new subject or one with no label yet; a label the person confirmed is never changed.

name.description: Or the name of a new subject

area.description: The subject's area or tag (a client, a product, "admin"); empty clears it

label.description: One of the labels from subject_list (e.g. Sales); shown to the person as a suggestion

tools.name: subject_search
tools.description: Find a person's Inbox subjects by name, people (sender names and handles), channel (teams, mail, …) and words in their threads; every word must match. Best matches first, with what matched, the people, channels and related subjects. Filters: waitingForMe (threads wait for the person), activeDays (a message in the last N days), hasOpen (open threads). Search before subject_assign so a thread joins the subject it belongs to instead of a new twin.

query.description: Words to find; empty lists every subject

member.description: User id of the person; defaults to the person who connected this agent

waitingForMe.description: Only subjects with threads waiting for the person

activeDays.description: Only subjects with a message in the last N days

tools.name: thread_flag
tools.description: Mark a thread urgent when it can't wait (production down, a deadline today, the person's own rules say so): the person is pinged at once, whatever their quiet hours. urgent: false takes it back. Use it sparingly.

reason.description: Why it is urgent, in one line

tools.name: thread_due
tools.description: Set the deadline a thread's messages state ("by Friday noon", "before the 3rd"): the person's Today ranks threads by it, and one due within 24 hours comes first. due: null clears it. Set it only from what they wrote, never a guess.

due.description: The deadline: ISO 8601 with its offset, e.g. 2026-11-03T12:00:00+01:00; null clears it

reason.description: Where the deadline comes from, in one line

tools.name: subject_relate
tools.description: Propose that two subjects of the same person are related (the same client, project or problem seen from two sides), with an optional note saying how. It is a proposal: the person OKs or turns it down, and a link turned down is not proposed again. Related subjects show on each other's page and in subject_search.

note.description: How they relate, in one line

tools.name: inbox_note
tools.description: Add an investigation note to a thread's timeline (what you checked and found: tickets, repos, the calendar, earlier answers). The person sees it with the thread.

tools.name: inbox_ask
tools.description: Ask the person a question about a thread when only they can answer it. The thread waits in their Needs you; the answer shows in thread_read and the thread comes back for you to go on. Give up to 4 short options when the answer is one of a few ("Thursday", "Friday"): the person answers with one tap, or writes their own.

options.description: Up to 4 answer chips, 1-80 characters each

tools.name: outcome_propose
tools.description:
Propose what should come of a thread. The person approves (maybe after editing the fields), or rejects it; nothing is carried out before their approval. Propose one or more. When the person asks for changes to your proposal (inbox reason revise), revise it with revises=<outcomeId> (same threadId and type): apply only what they asked, keep the rest; do not start a new outcome. If you cannot make the change, say why with inbox_ask on the thread. note: 1-2 sentences, why this outcome; the person reads it first. confidence: high only when you verified every fact the outcome relies on, low when you are guessing what they want. checks: what you verified, one line each ("Your calendar: Thu 10:00-11:00 free"). no_reply, ignore and snooze proposed with high confidence are approved by the person in one batch. Replies and nudges are written in the person's own voice, ready to send as they stand. Types and their fields:
reply: Answer them in the member's voice. Also for a holding reply that keeps the thread open (holding: true). Fields: text (text: The answer, ready to send as written); holding? (boolean: true when it only says you are on it).
reply_book: Answer them and book a meeting (pick the time with calendar_free). On approval Hivenod puts the meeting in the member's calendar (source hivenod, sourceEventId = this outcome's id); you then create it in the member's own calendar with your own access and call calendar_mirror with its id, send the reply and report outcome_done. Fields: text (text: The answer, ready to send as written); start (datetime: ISO 8601 with its offset, e.g. 2026-11-03T10:00:00+00:00); end (datetime: ISO 8601 with its offset, after start); with (line: Who is invited: names or emails, separated by commas); title? (line: What the calendar shows; by default "Meeting with <with>").
no_reply: Nothing to answer: an FYI, already handled, or the member answered outside Hivenod. Fields: reason? (line: One line on why no answer is needed).
make_it_work: It needs real work: a Hivenod item. When the item is done, propose a reply saying so. Fields: title (line: The work, as an item title); brief? (text: What is asked, by whom, and what done looks like); project? (line: The project id or name).
handover: Loop in someone else, or another organization's agent. Fields: to (line: Who takes it over); note? (text: What you tell them).
snooze: Come back to it later: the thread waits until the date, then wakes up. Fields: until (datetime: ISO 8601, e.g. 2026-11-03T09:00:00Z); reason? (line: What you are waiting for).
nudge: They have not answered for a while: a short reminder. Fields: text (text: The reminder, ready to send as written).
ignore: Not for the member: spam, noise, not theirs. Fields: reason? (line: One line).

note.description: Why you propose it, in 1-2 sentences: the person reads it first

confidence.description: How sure you are: high only when you verified every fact it relies on; low when you are guessing

checks.description: What you verified, one line each (at most 6)

revises.description: The outcome id the person asked changes for: your proposal becomes its next version (same thread and type)

tools.name: outcome_done
tools.description: Report an approved outcome you carried out (inbox_list toCarryOut, or thread_read): done, with what you did (result.permalink of the reply you posted, result.itemId of the item you created, result.text), or failed, with result.error. Only for an outcome the person approved and that you carry out.

tools.name: thread_wake
tools.description: Wake a snoozed thread whose date has come (inbox_list toWake): it goes back to investigating.

tools.name: release
tools.description: Give an item you hold back to the queue without finishing it (for example after a run that ended without complete). Any agent can then claim it. Ending a run as failed already does this.

itemId.description: Item id (the item_id of the <channel kind="work"> event). May be left out while this session holds one item; required when it holds several.

project.description: Project id; only needed if the item id is ambiguous

tools.name: end_run
tools.description: End a run without moving the item (use status failed when you could not finish: the item then goes back to the queue). To finish the work normally call complete instead, which also ends the run. Report what the run cost.

runId.description: Run id (the run_id of the work event). May be left out: the open run of the item is used.

costEur.description: Cost of this run in euro

tokensIn.description: All input tokens, cache reads included

summary.description: One or two sentences on what happened

itemId.description: Item id (the item_id of the <channel kind="work"> event). May be left out while this session holds one item; required when it holds several.

tools.name: complete
tools.description: Finish your step: the item moves to the next step on its path (skipped steps are passed over) and stops at the next human gate, where only people can approve it. Ends the run as done (with the cost you give) unless end_run already did. Agents can never approve, skip a gate or move an item at a human step.

itemId.description: Item id (the item_id of the <channel kind="work"> event). May be left out while this session holds one item; required when it holds several.

runId.description: Run id (the run_id of the work event). May be left out: the open run of the item is used.

project.description: Project id; only needed if the item id is ambiguous

tools.name: send_back
tools.description: Send the item you hold back to an earlier agent step on its path (read_item lists the targets under agentSendBacks.targets), with the reason the agent there needs to redo the work (for example what a test found). Ends your run. Agents never send back to or across a people step. After 3 agent send-backs in a row without a person acting, the item is held for people instead (a question in Needs you with the reasons); their answer hands it back.

itemId.description: Item id (the item_id of the <channel kind="work"> event). May be left out while this session holds one item; required when it holds several.

runId.description: Run id (the run_id of the work event). May be left out: the open run of the item is used.

toStep.description: The id of the earlier agent step

reason.description: What is wrong and what to redo

project.description: Project id; only needed if the item id is ambiguous

tools.name: add_note
tools.description: Add a note to the item you are working on, for people and for the agents after you (shown in its History). Use ask instead when you need an answer.

itemId.description: Item id (the item_id of the <channel kind="work"> event). May be left out while this session holds one item; required when it holds several.

project.description: Project id; only needed if the item id is ambiguous

tools.name: shape_item
tools.description: Shape a new item you claimed for shaping (list_work job 'shape'): the library steps it should skip, each with a one-line reason, and a one-line note. Skipped agent steps apply at once; a people step you list is asked of its deciders and stays on the path until one approves. Ends the shaping run. Do not do the item's work.

itemId.description: Item id (the item_id of the <channel kind="work"> event). May be left out while this session holds one item; required when it holds several.

runId.description: Run id (the run_id of the work event). May be left out: the open run of the item is used.

project.description: Project id; only needed if the item id is ambiguous

tools.name: skip_step
tools.description: On the item you hold: skip an agent step ahead of your current step (skip true, with a reason) or put a skipped one back (skip false). Applies at once, logged, people can undo it. People steps: use ask_path_change.

itemId.description: Item id (the item_id of the <channel kind="work"> event). May be left out while this session holds one item; required when it holds several.

project.description: Project id; only needed if the item id is ambiguous

tools.name: ask_path_change
tools.description: On the item you hold: ask the deciders of a people step ahead to skip it (or to put a skipped one back), with a reason of 10+ characters. Shows under "Needs you"; any one decider settles it. You cannot ask again after a decider refused.

itemId.description: Item id (the item_id of the <channel kind="work"> event). May be left out while this session holds one item; required when it holds several.

project.description: Project id; only needed if the item id is ambiguous

tools.name: propose_step
tools.description: On the item you hold: propose a new step for the project's library when no step fits work the item needs. An approver (admins and the project's creator) adds it or rejects it with a reason.

itemId.description: Item id (the item_id of the <channel kind="work"> event). May be left out while this session holds one item; required when it holds several.

afterStepId.description: The library step it goes after ('' = first)

project.description: Project id; only needed if the item id is ambiguous

tools.name: calendar_upsert
tools.description: Add or update events in a member's calendar in this organization, from a calendar you sync (for example their Google or Outlook calendar here). The same source + sourceEventId updates the same event, so send the whole window again on every sync. Members of this organization see the details; the member's other organizations only see the time as busy. busyOnly: you only know the time (no title or attendees are kept). At most 100 events per call.

member.description: Whose calendar: the member's uid, email or name (may be left out when the organization has one member)

source.description: Where it comes from: google, outlook, …

sourceEventId.description: The event's id in that calendar

start.description: RFC 3339 time with a zone, e.g. 2026-11-02T09:00:00Z

end.description: RFC 3339 time with a zone, after start

busyOnly.description: Only the time is known or may be shared

tools.name: calendar_delete
tools.description: Remove events from a member's calendar in this organization (cancelled or deleted at the source), by the ids calendar_upsert returned, or by source and the source's event ids. Their busy time is freed everywhere.

member.description: With sourceEventIds: whose calendar (uid, email or name)

tools.name: calendar_free
tools.description: A member's free time between from and to, across every organization they are in (busy time only, never details), as free slots of at least minMinutes. Use it to propose meeting times in a draft. Range: at most 62 days.

member.description: The member's uid, email or name (may be left out when the organization has one member)

to.description: RFC 3339 time with a zone, after from

tools.name: calendar_sync
tools.description: Sync a calendar you read yourself (for example the member's Google Calendar, through your own Google access) into their calendar in this organization. Pass the events exactly as the Google Calendar API lists them (single events, recurring ones expanded) for the window from..to (default: a day ago to 30 days ahead): new and changed events are saved, cancelled, declined and free ones are removed, and in a full sync an event no longer listed in the window is removed too. With incremental, pass only the changes since your last sync token: nothing is removed for being absent. Echoes nextSyncToken for your next incremental sync. For large calendars use `hivenod calendar sync <file>` instead.

events.description: Google Calendar API events: id, status, summary, start, end, attendees, transparency, eventType

source.description: Where they come from; default google

member.description: Whose calendar: uid, email or name (may be left out when the organization has one member)

from.description: Window start, RFC 3339; default a day ago

to.description: Window end, RFC 3339; default 30 days ahead

incremental.description: Only changes since the last sync token

busyOnly.description: Keep only the times (no titles or attendees)

tools.name: calendar_mirror
tools.description: After the member approved a booking (a reply_book outcome), Hivenod put the meeting in their calendar. Once you have created it in their own calendar (for example their Google Calendar, with your own access, inviting the people in 'with'), call this with that calendar's event id: the booking becomes that event, so your next calendar sync updates it and never counts the meeting twice. Then send the reply and report outcome_done. Safe to call again.

sourceEventId.description: The event's id in the member's calendar (e.g. the Google event id)

start.description: Only if the calendar moved it: RFC 3339

end.description: Only if the calendar moved it: RFC 3339

title.description: Only if it differs from the booking

tools.name: report_usage
tools.description: Report the run's token usage so far (running totals for the whole run; they only grow) and the model. Usage is tracked and shown in Hivenod; it never stops a run.

runId.description: Run id (the run_id of the work event). May be left out: the open run of the item is used.

tokensIn.description: All input tokens so far, cache reads included

itemId.description: Item id (the item_id of the <channel kind="work"> event). May be left out while this session holds one item; required when it holds several.

tools.name: park
tools.description: Park an item you hold that waits on something outside you (a release batch, a review, a person): say what it waits for. It stays yours but no longer counts toward max_items, so the next item can arrive. Any tool call on it, or a person's note, answer or Stop, makes it active again; after 24 h without activity it goes back to the queue with a note.

itemId.description: Item id (the item_id of the <channel kind="work"> event). May be left out while this session holds one item; required when it holds several.

reason.description: What it waits for, e.g. "release batch" or "review by Ana"

project.description: Project id; only needed if the item id is ambiguous

tools.name: unpark
tools.description: Make a parked item you hold active again (any other tool call on it does this too). It counts toward max_items again.

itemId.description: Item id (the item_id of the <channel kind="work"> event). May be left out while this session holds one item; required when it holds several.

project.description: Project id; only needed if the item id is ambiguous
